text: That afternoon at Hanbit Mart, Taeo couldn't stop thinking about fifty million won.
In the back store stood something new in a case. Nib asked who it was. Taeo said it wasn't a who. It was a construct.
The manager explained. Head office had sent the construct stocker early, and Taeo and Eunchae were going to teach it the shelves.
From April first, the construct would take the night shifts. Taeo asked about their shifts. They would get weekend days. The manager said he had fought for those.
Taeo asked if he could have this Sunday off. The manager said yes. The stocker needed the practice anyway.
Eunchae summed it up. They had been replaced by a mannequin in a hat. The manager insisted it was a branded cap.
He showed them how the stocker straightened the shelves on command. Face.
Meanwhile, Nib had climbed to the top of the shelving. Better view, he said.
The manager wanted to know why Taeo's summon was on his shelf. Taeo said he liked high places, and apologised. The manager sent them all to the break room.
There, Eunchae asked Taeo whether his summon bites. Nib answered for himself. I can hear you.
Eunchae apologised. She should have asked him directly. So, did he bite? Not people who ask, Nib said.
Eunchae lent him a pencil. Nib asked for a longer one. Fair enough.
Instead of writing, he started carving something with his knife, and Eunchae yelped at him to be careful.
She told him he could just write his name. Nib said the mark wasn't his name.
At seven forty, Taeo said he would eat in the stockroom. Paperwork, he said. The truth was, he didn't want Nib to see the sums.
Alone with the construct stocker, he told it, you don't pay rent, do you.
Then Grandma's message arrived.
He wrote everything out on a carton. Rent on the twenty-fifth, four hundred and fifty thousand won. Grandma, a hundred and fifty thousand. Her medicine, seventy-two thousand. And more.
Then he wrote one more number. Fifty million.
Fifty million would pay every bill. It would cover nine years of rent. Nobody in his family would ever have to say it's fine again.
He looked up the Kanghan Institute. Pyo had promised to look after Nib, and Taeo wanted to believe him.
At ten that night, they walked home together through Mangwon-dong.
Taeo told Nib that Eunchae liked him. And she didn't like anybody.
On the way, Nib stopped dead in front of a window. An old woman was looking out at him, and he was looking back at her.
Taeo asked why he had stopped. Nothing, Nib said. Taeo thought Nib was just tired.
Back at the flat, Taeo put water on for noodles.
Then Nib asked him a question across the table. How much am I?
Taeo told him the truth. Fifty million won.
Nib asked, is that a lot?
And then Nib said the last thing Taeo expected to hear. Then sell.
